correctness.rationale: Exact cuboctahedron facets and opposite-visibility edge counts give the almost-sure 6/8 chamber law. Girard computes chamber area. Cauchy gives the directionwise projected area and total mean; spherical boundary-flux integration over the exact triangle gives E[B 1_{N=8}]=3, with remainder sqrt(3). An exact rational lower bound for p proves negative covariance. The bundled 500 convex-hull reconstructions, 5184-node quadrature, and 240000 sampling checks were actually executed, but analytic steps—not finite tests—prove the claims.

originality.rationale: The unweighted count and octagon marginal are already implied by McGuire 2004; these are acknowledged prior and not offered as independent originality. The principal new mathematical claim is the explicitly integrated area-weighted silhouette split, conditional area inversion, and negative mixed covariance for the cuboctahedron. Relevant primary results on silhouettes, reconstruction, and random-shadow vertex bounds were compared by implication and did not state or dominate this weighted moment. Historical priority outside the inspected sources remains uncertain.

value.rationale: A canonical Archimedean polyhedron has an exact, complete silhouette-type partition and two exact projected-area budgets 3 and sqrt(3). Conditioning by a geometric image-complexity observable reverses naive area–complexity ordering, a substantive naturally motivated correlation. This is neither a generic numerical exercise nor a restatement of marginal mean formulas: it evaluates a mixed statistic requiring geometric chamber integration.
